epithet: “We sent down the Reminder, and We shall guard it”
lede: They called him a madman and asked where his angels were. The reply has stood for fourteen centuries: “It is We who sent down the Reminder, and it is We who shall guard it.” Then the surah gives him a gift — seven oft-repeated ayat, and the mighty Qurʾan — and tells him to say it out loud.

names.name: al-Ḥijr
names.note: After the people of al-Ḥijr (15:80–84): Thamūd, who carved their houses in the cliffs, north of Madinah on the road to Syria. The Prophet ﷺ passed their ruins on the way to Tabūk.

revelation.detail: Ibn al-Jawzī says it is Makkan, all of it, without any disagreement he knew of, and Ibn Kathīr heads it Makkan. The traditional order places it fifty-fourth, directly after Yūsuf.

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ الحِجْرِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها مِن غَيْرِ خِلافٍ نَعْلَمُهُ

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ النَّحّاسُ في «ناسِخِهِ»، وابْنُ مَرْدُوَيْهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ الحِجْرِ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by al-Naḥḥās and Ibn Mardawayh.

attested.quote: هي مَكِّيَّةٌ بِالِاتِّفاقِ كَما قالَ القُرْطُبِيُّ

setting: It opens with a sentence about the future that no one in Makkah would then have credited: “Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they had been Muslims.” For the present, the instruction is to leave them alone — “let them eat and enjoy themselves, and let hope distract them; they will come to know.”

What they were saying is quoted: “You, upon whom the Reminder has been sent down — you are surely mad. Why do you not bring us the angels, if you are truthful?” The answer comes in two parts. The angels are not sent down except with the truth, and when they come there is no more respite. And as for the Reminder: “It is We who sent it down, and it is We who shall guard it.” Every earlier scripture had been entrusted to its people to keep. This one, alone, Allah takes upon Himself.

Then the surah does what the Makkan surahs do: it widens the frame until the mockers look small. The sky with its constellations, guarded against every devil. The earth spread out, and everything in it weighed. “There is not a thing but its storehouses are with Us, and We send it down only in a known measure.” Behind the mockers stands an older one. Iblīs refuses to bow to a creature made of dried clay, and is given respite, and says: “I shall make things seem fair to them on earth, and mislead them all — except Your chosen servants among them.” The reply is the believer’s charter: “Over My servants you have no authority.”

At its centre the surah gives a two-sided announcement, and at once illustrates both sides. “Tell My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful — and that My punishment is the painful punishment.” The same angels come to Ibrāhīm with news of a son, and go on to the towns of Lūṭ. “Who despairs of the mercy of his Lord but those who are astray?”

Its last passage is spoken directly to the Prophet ﷺ. “We have given you seven of the oft-repeated, and the mighty Qurʾan” — so do not look with longing at what others have been given. “So proclaim what you are commanded, and turn away from the idolaters. We are enough for you against the mockers.” And then, with a tenderness that is easy to miss: “We know that your breast is straitened by what they say. So glorify your Lord with praise, and be among those who prostrate, and worship your Lord until the certain end comes to you.”
aim: To warn those who deny of the punishment, by showing scenes of those who were destroyed — as a caution to those addressed, and to steady the believers.
themes: The sky guarded, the earth weighed
“Over My servants you have no authority”

outline.title: The Reminder
outline.summary: Alif Lām Rā. These are the ayat of the Book, and of a clear Qurʾan. Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they had been Muslims. Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves. They say: “You, upon whom the Reminder has been sent down, you are surely mad.” It is We who sent down the Reminder, and it is We who shall guard it (15:9). Even if We opened to them a gate of heaven and they kept ascending through it, they would say: “Our eyes have been dazzled; we are a people bewitched.”

outline.title: Sky, earth and storehouses
outline.summary: We have set constellations in the sky and made it fair to those who look, and guarded it from every outcast devil. The earth We have spread out, and cast into it firm mountains, and caused to grow in it everything in due balance. There is not a thing but its storehouses are with Us, and We send it down only in a known measure. We send the winds to fertilise. It is We who give life and cause death, and We are the inheritors.

outline.title: Clay, and the one who would not bow
outline.summary: We created man from dried clay, from moulded mud, and the jinn We created before, from scorching fire. Your Lord said to the angels: “When I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down in prostration to him.” All bowed, except Iblīs. “My Lord, because You have sent me astray, I shall make things seem fair to them, and mislead them all — except Your chosen servants.” — “Over My servants you have no authority.” Hell has seven gates. The mindful are among gardens and springs: “Enter in peace, secure.”

outline.title: Mercy and punishment
outline.summary: Tell My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment. Tell them of the guests of Ibrāhīm: “We give you good news of a knowing boy.” — “Who despairs of the mercy of his Lord but those who are astray?” The messengers came to the family of Lūṭ: “Set out with your family in a part of the night.” The blast seized them at sunrise. In that are signs for those who read the marks. The people of the Thicket were wrongdoers; and the people of al-Ḥijr denied the messengers, hewing houses from the mountains, feeling secure.

outline.title: The gift, and the command
outline.summary: We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth; the Hour is surely coming, so pardon with a gracious pardon. We have given you seven of the oft-repeated, and the mighty Qurʾan. Do not stretch your eyes towards what We have given some of them to enjoy; and lower your wing to the believers. So proclaim what you are commanded. We are enough for you against the mockers. We know that your breast is straitened by what they say; so glorify your Lord with praise, and worship your Lord until the certain end comes to you.

keyAyah.why: The promise on which every reader of the Qurʾan depends: its preservation is undertaken by the One who sent it down.

virtues.text: “The Mother of the Qurʾan is the seven oft-repeated, and the mighty Qurʾan.”
virtues.arabic: أُمُّ الْقُرْآنِ هِيَ السَّبْعُ الْمَثَانِي وَالْقُرْآنُ الْعَظِيمُ

virtues.text: Abū Saʿīd ibn al-Muʿallā said: the Prophet ﷺ said to me, “Shall I not teach you the greatest surah in the Qurʾan before I leave the mosque?” Then, as he was about to leave, I reminded him, and he said: “‘Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds’ — it is the seven oft-repeated, and the mighty Qurʾan that I have been given.”

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions as they passed al-Ḥijr: “Do not enter upon these people who were punished, unless you are weeping. If you are not weeping, do not enter upon them, lest there befall you what befell them.”

virtuesNote: Ibn Kathīr notes that the Companions differed over what “the seven oft-repeated” are. Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās are among those reported to have said: the seven long surahs. The hadith above, in al-Bukhārī, identifies them as al-Fātiḥah; Ibn Kathīr calls it an explicit text on the matter, while allowing that the description may extend to the long surahs as well.
before: Sūrat Ibrāhīm ended with a warning to mankind of a Day when the wrongdoers will ask for a little more time. Al-Ḥijr begins there: they will wish they had been Muslims.
after: Al-Ḥijr ends: “worship your Lord until the certain end comes to you.” Al-Naḥl begins: “The command of Allah has come; so do not seek to hasten it.”
